slot.brief: Give a named-reaction description (Cannizzaro) and ask the products from a given aldehyde lacking α-H; identify major/minor products.

stem: The Cannizzaro reaction between formaldehyde and 2,2-dimethylpropanal in the presence of conc. NaOH produces

verdicts.working: Formaldehyde is oxidized to sodium formate while 2,2-dimethylpropanal is reduced to neopentyl alcohol in the crossed Cannizzaro reaction.

working:
Both aldehydes lack α‑H. In a cross Cannizzaro reaction, formaldehyde is always oxidized to formate (HCOO⁻), while the other aldehyde is reduced to the corresponding alcohol. Here 2,2‑dimethylpropanal is reduced to neopentyl alcohol. Hence the products are sodium formate and neopentyl alcohol.

Independent check: Formaldehyde is oxidized to sodium formate while 2,2-dimethylpropanal is reduced to neopentyl alcohol in the crossed Cannizzaro reaction.
solution:
Both aldehydes lack an $alpha$-hydrogen, so they undergo crossed Cannizzaro reaction. Formaldehyde is oxidized to formate, while 2,2-dimethylpropanal is reduced to neopentyl alcohol:
$$\mathrm{HCHO + (CH_3)_3CCHO + NaOH \rightarrow HCOONa + (CH_3)_3CCH_2OH}$$
